newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall on profit-taking, volume modest.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall on profit-taking, volume modest.

text.p: French shares fell on Tuesday, weighed down by profit taking and concerns about a sharp fall in London equities on fears of higher British interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 17.85 points or 0.61 percent at 2,929.81. The CAC-40 July futures contract fell 19 points to 2,936.
Volume was a modest 7.19 billion francs and brokers said activity was calming down with the start of the school holidays in France.

Shares in electronic engineering and telecommunications giant Alcatel Alsthom fell 2.02 percent to 775 francs. Chairman Serge Tchuruk told Reuters he was waiting to hear more details of GEC's plans to de-merge the GEC Alsthom rail and power joint venture.
GEC said on Tuesday that its plan may include a flotation. A leading French broker estimated GEC Alsthom's market capitalisation at 45 billion francs.
A GEC Alsthom flotation could help fund Alcatel's bid for Thomson-CSF. The defence electronics firm's stock closed up 3.16 percent at 172.90 francs.
Shares in Eurotunnel rose 3.66 percent to 8.50 francs, as the market bet shareholders would approve a debt restructuring plan for the Channel Tunnel operator at a meeting on Thursday.
